;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[War in Afghanistan (2001–2021)]]
**[[17 September 2019 Afghanistan bombings]]
***[[Suicide bombing]]s in [[Afghanistan]] kill 48 people including civilians and soldiers. The first is in [[Charikar]] at a rally for [[Ashraf Ghani]], the [[President of Afghanistan]]. The second is in [[Kabul]] near the [[Embassy of the United States, Kabul|U.S. embassy]]. [https://www.nytimes.com/2019/09/17/world/asia/afghanistan-bombing-ghani.html (''The New York Times'')] [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-49726088 (BBC News)]
*[[Islamic terrorism in Europe]]
**An Italian soldier in [[Milan]] was stabbed in the neck and in the back with a pair of scissors by a man. He was arrested after the stabbing, which was described as a terrorist attack linked to Islamic extremism. The soldier survived the attack. [https://www.tgcom24.mediaset.it/cronaca/lombardia/milano-ferisce-un-militare-e-poi-urla-allah-akbar-arrestato-per-attentato-terroristico_3232392-201902a.shtml (TGCOM24)]

;Arts and culture
*[[Bartholomew I of Constantinople|Ecumenical Patriarch Bartholomew]] meets with [[Pope Francis]] at the Vatican. In his brief remarks, Patriarch Bartholomew talks about the value of [[Synod|synodality]] in the [[Eastern Orthodox Church]]. [https://www.vaticannews.va/en/pope/news/2019-09/pope-francis-meets-orthodox-patriarch-bartholomew.html (Vatican News)]

;Disasters and accidents
*[[2019 Atlantic hurricane season]]
**[[2019 Atlantic hurricane season#Tropical Storm Imelda|Tropical Storm Imelda]] makes landfall in [[Texas]], threatening severe flash flooding throughout [[Eastern Texas]] and the [[Houston]] area. [https://www.washingtonpost.com/weather/2019/09/17/houston-braces-up-foot-rain-unnamed-tropical-weather-system/ (''The Washington Post'')]
*Italian champion speedboat designer and racer [[Fabio Buzzi]] and two other racers  are killed when their boat, attempting to set a new [[Monte Carlo]]-to-[[Venice]] record in the  Assonautica Italiana race, crashes into a sunken, flood-barrier dam near the finish line. A fourth racer is in hospital with serious injuries. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-49738385 (BBC News)]  [https://ilglobo.com.au/news/45141/motorboat-racer-fabio-buzzi-one-of-three-killed-in-boat-crash-in-venice/# (''Il Globo'')]

;International relations
*[[Foreign relations of Taiwan]], [[Foreign relations of China]], [[Foreign relations of the Solomon Islands]]
**[[President of Taiwan|Taiwanese President]] [[Tsai Ing-wen]] regrets and strongly condemns the move by the [[Solomon Islands]] to cut ties with [[Taiwan]] and establish relations with [[China]]. [https://www.rnz.co.nz/international/pacific-news/398932/taiwan-condemns-solomons-china-switch (RNZ)]
*[[2019 Abqaiq–Khurais attack]]
**An anonymous U.S. official says the United States is certain that the attack was launched from [[Iran]]ian territory and that it involved [[cruise missile]]s. [http://www.dailystar.com.lb/News/Middle-East/2019/Sep-17/491769-kingdom-is-capable-of-responding-to-attacks-king-salman.ashx (''The Daily Star'')]

;Politics and elections
*[[Efforts to impeach Donald Trump#Start of formal impeachment proceedings|Donald Trump impeachment hearings]]
**Amid a [[gag order]] from the [[White House]], [[Impeachment in the United States|impeachment]] hearings begin at the [[United States House Committee on the Judiciary]]. [https://www.independent.co.uk/news/world/americas/us-politics/trump-news-live-impeachment-hearing-la-today-california-twitter-bay-area-tax-returns-a9108946.html (''The Independent'')]
*[[Brexit]], [[2019 British prorogation controversy]]
**The [[Supreme Court of the United Kingdom|UK Supreme Court]] begins considering the lawfulness of [[Prime Minister of the United Kingdom|Prime Minister]] [[Boris Johnson]]'s [[Prorogation in the United Kingdom#Boris Johnson (2019)|prorogation]] of [[Parliament of the United Kingdom|Parliament]]. It is jointly considering two appeals. One is against a ruling by the [[High Court of Justice|High Court]] under [[English law]] that the issue is solely a matter for the Prime Minister and one the courts do not have jurisdiction over. The other is against a ruling by the [[Court of Session]] under [[Scots law]] declaring the suspension unlawful and a nullity, and requiring Johnson to recall Parliament. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-politics-49722087 (BBC News)]
*[[April 2019 Spanish general election]], [[Politics of Spain]]
**[[Prime Minister of Spain|Spanish Prime Minister]] [[Pedro Sánchez]], after failing to achieve support from the [[Unidas Podemos]] alliance, announces the calling for a snap [[November 2019 Spanish general election|election on 10 November]], which would be the fourth general election in 4 years. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-spain-politics/spain-to-hold-snap-election-on-november-10-after-party-talks-fail-idUSKBN1W20VG (Reuters)] [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-49736118?intlink_from_url=https://www.bbc.com/news/topics/c5wdv20l9zzt/pedro-sanchez&link_location=live-reporting-story (BBC News)]
*[[September 2019 Israeli legislative election]]
**[[Israel|Israeli]] voters head to the polls after [[April 2019 Israeli legislative election|the last election]] failed to form [[Cabinet of Israel|a government]]. Exit polls show the incumbent right-wing [[Likud]] barely losing to the centrist [[Blue and White (political alliance)|Blue and White alliance]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-israel-election/israeli-election-too-close-to-call-netanyahu-weakened-exit-polls-idUSKBN1W12UY (Reuters)]
**The [[Arab citizens of Israel|Arab]]-dominated [[Joint List]] is projected to win between 13 and 15 seats, its highest showing ever. [[Yisrael Beiteinu]], led by former [[Ministry of Defense (Israel)|Defense Minister]] [[Avigdor Lieberman]], is expected to play kingmaker. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-israel-election/israels-netanyahu-teetering-in-close-election-race-polls-idUSKBN1W300B?il=0 (Reuters)]
*[[2019 Venezuelan presidential crisis]]
**The Venezuelan secret service releases [[National Assembly (Venezuela)|National Assembly]] Vice President [[Edgar Zambrano]]. The [[Nicolás Maduro]] government says his release comes after a partial compromise with members of [[Juan Guaidó]]'s opposition government to live peacefully; Guaidó says the Maduro government has been forced to release him under international human rights pressure. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-latin-america-49736985 (BBC News)]

;Science and technology
*[[Christchurch mosque shootings]]
**Following the attack, which was [[livestreaming|livestreamed]] on [[Facebook]], the [[social network]] teams up with the [[Metropolitan Police]] of [[London]]. Facebook is providing [[bodycam]]s to the force's firearms officers to help train its [[artificial intelligence]] systems, enabling it to automatically detect and remove live first-person footage of violent incidents. The company says it previously had insufficient footage for its software to suitably match fresh footage with, and has been criticised for its role in the shooting. [[Instagram]] say they will also participate. [https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2019/sep/17/facebook-teams-up-with-police-to-stop-live-streaming-of-terror-attacks (''The Guardian'')]
